items.stem: A price column is heavily skewed by a few very large values. Which measure best represents a typical value?

options.rationale: Correct: the median resists skew and extreme values better than the mean.
The mean is pulled toward the extreme values in a skewed distribution.
The maximum is one extreme value, not a typical one.
The sum is a total, not a measure of a typical value.

items.explanation: Correct: the median resists skew and extreme values better than the mean.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which of the following are sound reasons to prefer the median over the mean in a report? (Select TWO)

options.text: The data is skewed by a few extreme values
options.rationale: Correct: the median is robust to skew and outliers.

options.text: A small number of outliers would distort the average
options.rationale: Correct: outliers pull the mean but barely move the median.

options.text: You want the total across all records
options.rationale: A total calls for the sum, not the median.

options.text: The data is perfectly symmetric with no outliers
options.rationale: When data is symmetric with no outliers, mean and median agree and either is fine.

items.explanation: Correct: the median is robust to skew and outliers.

items.stem: Two variables rise together across a dataset. What is the safest conclusion?

options.text: They are correlated, but this alone does not prove one causes the other
options.rationale: Correct: correlation does not establish causation without further evidence.
Co-movement alone cannot establish a causal direction.
They are clearly related; the question is whether the relationship is causal.
Correlation between variables is common and does not imply an error.

items.explanation: Correct: correlation does not establish causation without further evidence.
